'''Klavdija Kutnar''' (born December 23, 1980) is a [[Slovenes|Slovene]] [[mathematician]]. She received her PhD at the [[University of Primorska]] (UP) in 2008, and she currently serves as the Rector of the university.

== Biography ==

Klavdija Kutnar was born 23 December 1980, in [[Ljubljana]], [[Slovenia]]. She graduated from the Faculty of Education of the [[University of Ljubljana]] in 2003, and in 2008 received her PhD in mathematics at the University of Primorska under the supervision of [[Dragan Marušič]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Strukturne lastnosti simetričnih grafov : doktorska disertacija|url=https://repozitorij.upr.si/IzpisGradiva.php?id=8933&lang=eng|publisher=University of Primorska, Faculty of Mathematics, Science and Information Technologies|date=2008|degree=thesis|first=Klavdija|last=Kutnar}}</ref> From 2010 to 2012 she was head of the Department of Mathematics at the University of Primorska Institute Andrej Marušič (UP IAM). In 2012, she was elected dean of the University of Primorska Faculty of Mathematics, Natural Sciences and Information Technology (UP FAMNIT) and since 2015 has concurrently been assistant director of UP IAM. In 2018 she was granted the titles of Research Counsellor and Full Professor in Mathematics at the [[University of Primorska]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/users/klavdija-kutnar|title=Klavdija Kutnar {{!}} EMS|website=euro-math-soc.eu|language=en|access-date=2019-04-23|archive-date=2019-04-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423074926/https://euro-math-soc.eu/users/klavdija-kutnar|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2019 she was elected the fourth rector of the University of Primorska.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.delo.si/novice/slovenija/nova-rektorica-univerze-na-primorskem-je-prof-dr-klavdija-kutnar-253655.html|title=Nova rektorica Univerze na Primorskem je prof. dr. Klavdija Kutnar|last=P|first=J. B.|date=2019-11-26|website=www.delo.si|language=sl-si|access-date=2019-11-27}}</ref>

== Research ==
Kutnar's main research area is [[algebraic graph theory]]. At the beginning of her research career, she also worked in [[mathematical chemistry]]. She is noted for her contribution to the study of the structural properties of particular families of symmetric graphs and in particular, her role in developing the original method of embedding graphs on surfaces to solve special cases of the well-known [[Lovász conjecture]]: the problem of finding [[Hamiltonian path]]s and cycles in [[Vertex-transitive graph|vertex-transitive]] and [[Cayley graph]]s. She is a member of the research program P1-0285, financed by the Slovenian Research and Innovation Agency (ARIS) and led by [[Dragan Marušič]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://p1-0285.iam.upr.si/en|title=UP IAM|website=p1-0285.iam.upr.si|language=en|access-date=2019-04-16}}</ref> In 2018, she was the first Slovenian female mathematician to obtain a basic research project financed by the ARIS (J1-9110).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://p1-0285.iam.upr.si/en/research-projects/j1-9110|title=UP IAM|website=p1-0285.iam.upr.si|language=en|access-date=2019-04-16}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==

* H. H. Glover, K. Kutnar, A. Malnič and D. Marušič, Hamilton cycles in (2, odd, 3)-Cayley graphs, Proc. London Math. Soc., 104 (Issue 6) (2012), 1171–1197, [https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1112/plms/pdr042 doi:10.1112/plms/pdr042]. 
* K. Kutnar and D. Marušič, Hamilton paths and cycles in vertex-transitive graphs - current directions, Discrete Math. 309 (Issue 17) (2009), 5491–5500, [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0012365X09000661?via%3Dihub doi:10.1016/j.disc.2009.02.017]. &nbsp;
* K. Kutnar and D. Marušič, A complete classification of cubic symmetric graphs of girth 6, J. Combin. Theory Ser B 99 (Issue 1) (2009), 162–184, [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0095895608000658?via%3Dihub doi: 10.1016/j.jctb.2008.06.001]. 
* K. Kutnar and D. Marušič, Odd extensions of transitive groups via symmetric graphs – the cubic case, J. Combin. Theory, Ser. B 136 (2019) 170–192, [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S009589561830100X doi.org/10.1016/j.jctb.2018.10.003].

== Professional work ==
Kutnar has been a member of the editorial board of the journal ''[[Ars Mathematica Contemporanea]]'' since 2016, serving as editor-in-chief from 2018. She is also a member of the editorial boards of the ''Bulletin of the Institute of Combinatorics and its Applications'' and ''[[Algebraic Combinatorics (journal)|Algebraic Combinatorics]],'' and managing editor of the scientific journal ''ADAM – The Art of Discrete and Applied Mathematics''.

She was a Deputy Chair of the Organizing Committee of the 8th [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in 2021, and a member of International Advisory Committee for the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] 2022, originally scheduled to take place in [[Saint Petersburg|St. Petersburg]], [[Russia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm/next-icm|title=Next ICM {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU)|website=www.mathunion.org|access-date=2019-04-16}}</ref>

She is a founding member and the secretary of the Slovenian Discrete and Applied Mathematics Society. Since 2017, she has been a member of the Council of the InnoRenew CoE (Center of Excellence for research and innovation in the field of renewable materials and a healthy living environment),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://innorenew.eu/about/institute|title=InnoRenew CoE – Institute|website=InnoRenew CoE|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-16}}</ref> and the leader of the investment project “Renewable Materials and Healthy Environments Research and Innovation Center of Excellence – InnoRenew CoE” at UP FAMNIT.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://innorenew.eu/about/project|title=InnoRenew CoE – Project|website=InnoRenew CoE|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-16}}</ref>

In 2017, Kutnar was appointed by the Minister to the Working Group to support the Peer-Counseling Project on the financing of higher education in Slovenia. She is also a member of the Council of the Republic of Slovenia for prizes and awards for outstanding achievements in science, research and development.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mizs.gov.si/si/delovna_podrocja/direktorat_za_znanost/sektor_za_znanost/dejavnost/nagrade_in_priznanja_za_izjemne_dosezke_v_znanstveno_raziskovalni_in_razvojni_dejavnosti/zois_awards/|title=Zois awards{{!}} Ministrstvo za izobraževanje, znanost in šport|website=www.mizs.gov.si|access-date=2019-04-16|archive-date=2019-04-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416093808/http://www.mizs.gov.si/si/delovna_podrocja/direktorat_za_znanost/sektor_za_znanost/dejavnost/nagrade_in_priznanja_za_izjemne_dosezke_v_znanstveno_raziskovalni_in_razvojni_dejavnosti/zois_awards/|url-status=dead}}</ref> &nbsp;In 2019, she became the President of the Council of the Republic of Slovenia for Higher Education.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.upr.si/sl/medijski-center/novosti-in-obvestila/prof-dr-klavdija-kutnar-je-bila-na-danasnji-seji-vlade-rs-imen|title=Prof. dr. Klavdija Kutnar je bila na današnji seji Vlade RS imenovana za predsednico Sveta RS za visoko šolstvo|website=www.upr.si|language=sl|access-date=2019-04-16}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Klavdija Kutnar has a twin sister, [[Andreja Kutnar]], who received the 2018 Zois Award for important scientific achievements in the field of wood science, and is the director of the InnoRenew CoE.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mizs.gov.si/si/medijsko_sredisce/novica/10578/|title=Podeljene so Zoisove in Puhove nagrade ter priznanja 2018|website=www.mizs.gov.si|language=sl|access-date=2019-04-16|archive-date=2019-04-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416192851/http://www.mizs.gov.si/si/medijsko_sredisce/novica/10578/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
